newsitem.title: USA: Army agent probed if sex while pregnant possible.
newsitem.headline: Army agent probed if sex while pregnant possible.

text.p: The Army's chief criminal investigator in a major sex abuse case said Wednesday he sought an expert opinion to determine if it was possible for a woman to have sex on a couch while eight months pregnant.

"I wanted an expert analysis or opinion or a computer-generated model," special agent Jeffrey S. Hormann told a hearing. "I didn't personally know if it was possible. I didn't know if it was impossible in the exact position that she (the alleged victim) stated."
"I've never done that myself," he said.
But the pathologists consulted said they could not provide him with what he was looking for, Hormann said.
The comments came during testimony in a preliminary hearing on sexual misconduct charges against the Army's highest-ranking enlisted man.

Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney, 46, faced 18 charges including indecent assault, adultery and obstruction of justice in the latest of a series recent sex scandals that have rocked the U.S. armed services.

One of the alleged victims, Sgt. Christine A. Roy, 25, testified earlier in the hearing that she gave in to months of McKinney's advances and had unwanted sex with him on his couch while she was nearly eight months pregnant.
Humiliated, she said she intended to take the incident to her grave but later made a formal complaint.
Both McKinney and Roy are married, but not to each other. Adultery is a crime under the military code, and Roy was granted immunity before describing the incident to authorities.

Hormann said he consulted with the Armed Forces Institute of Pathology (AFIP) because he had concerns about Roy's account of the incident, in which she said she was near the arm rest on an overstuffed couch and that McKinney pulled her maternity pants half-way down before climbing on top of her for intercourse.
"They (at AFIP) said that's not what they do," Hormann said. "They deal in dead bodies."
Three other women have accused McKinney with sexual misconduct. McKinney denied all the charges.
